title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
abstract: arXiv:2611.08916v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. translated_title: 论do-演算在通用可识别性问题上的不完备性
translated_abstract: 摘要：我们研究了从任意给定的观测分布和/或干预分布集合中进行因果效应识别的问题，并将其称为通用可识别性。uID问题推广了现有的经典可识别性和广义可识别性问题，后者仅考虑了从单纯的观测分布或特定类型的干预分布中进行识别的问题。先前的研究已经建立了图判据来确定在ID和gID问题中因果效应何时可识别，此外还提出了利用do-演算和基本概率运算的算法来计算这些效应。因此，已有结果表明do-演算在这些问题上既是可靠的也是完备的。尽管有这些成熟的研究成果，但对于do-演算完备性的含义，目前尚不存在正式的定义。我们为do-演算的完备性提出了一个严格的正式化定义……
tldr: 本文为do-演算的完备性提出了严格的形式化定义，并指出在从任意观测与干预分布集合中进行因果效应识别的通用可识别性问题中，do-演算并不完备。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a rigorous formalization of do-calculus completeness and shows that do-calculus is incomplete for universal identifiability (uID), the problem of identifying causal effects from arbitrary sets of observational and/or interventional distributions.
